name: Nick Schultz
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Public Safety Committee
district: California State Assembly District 44 (Burbank, Glendale, La Crescenta, Sunland-Tujunga, North Hollywood, Sherman Oaks, Studio City, Toluca Lake, and Valley Village). Note: Schultz's prior elected office was Burbank City Council/Mayor, not Glendale, though Glendale is part of his current Assembly district. (Source: official Assembly biography, a44.asmdc.org.)
background: Schultz was born August 27, 1988. He holds a bachelor's degree and a J.D. from the University of Oregon, was admitted to the Oregon State Bar in 2013, and to the California State Bar in 2014. He describes himself as the first in his working-class family to graduate from college, raised by a single mother. He lives in Burbank with his wife, Allie, and their two children. (Sources: official Assembly biography, a44.asmdc.org; Wikipedia, used as a substitute source because Ballotpedia's page for Schultz could not be retrieved after repeated attempts.)

Before the Assembly, Schultz worked as a Deputy District Attorney in Lane County, Oregon, then joined the California Department of Justice as a Deputy Attorney General, first in the Health Quality Enforcement Section (2016) and later in the Special Prosecutions Section (2018 onward), where the Assembly bio states he prosecuted public corruption, human trafficking, and financial crimes and helped establish a Post-Conviction Review Unit to address wrongful convictions. He also served on the Los Feliz Neighborhood Council governing board (2018) and the Los Angeles Central Area Planning Commission (2018 to 2020). (Sources: official Assembly biography; Wikipedia.)

Schultz was elected to the Burbank City Council in November 2020 (placing second in the field with roughly 15.3% of the vote), served as Vice Mayor from December 2022 to December 2023, and as Mayor of Burbank from December 2023 until he left the council in November 2024. As mayor he focused on homelessness reduction, crime prevention, carbon-neutrality goals, and housing affordability measures the Assembly bio credits with producing more than 1,000 new units of low-income housing. He was elected to the Assembly in November 2024, winning the District 44 general election with about 65.9% of the vote against Republican Tony Rodriguez, and took office December 2, 2024. (Sources: official Assembly biography; Wikipedia.)

voting_record_highlights: AB 379 (2025 to 2026), amending prostitution-related provisions of the Penal and Civil Codes to strengthen penalties and survivor protections: Schultz was the lead author with Assemblymember Nguyen and principal coauthor Mark González. It passed the Senate 33 to 2 on July 14, 2025, and was signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on July 30, 2025 as Chapter 82, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 379.)

AB 1036 (2025 to 2026), amending Penal Code Section 1054.9 on postconviction discovery procedures: Schultz was the author. The Assembly concurred in Senate amendments 54 to 18 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Newsom signed it October 7, 2025 as Chapter 444, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 1036.)

AB 690 (2025 to 2026), amending Penal Code Section 987.2 and adding Section 987.7 on indigent-defense compensation: Schultz was the author. It passed the Assembly on final passage 59 to 11 on August 28, 2026, and was signed by Gov. Newsom on September 20, 2026 as Chapter 359, Statutes of 2026. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 690.)

SB 42 (2025 to 2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Schultz was one of six Assembly coauthors (alongside Bennett, Haney, Ortega, Rogers, Schiavo, and Solache). It was signed by Gov. Newsom on October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Assemblymember Schultz was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. CalMatters' Digital Democracy tool, which publishes vote-alignment and bill-passage data for many legislators (used for Sen. Ben Allen's profile, for example), does not appear to have a profile page for Schultz as of this writing (the expected URL pattern returned a 404), so that source could not be used here either.
